Commentary.Commentary: The revised DLS score for India Under-19 is 130 in 37 overs. The Kiwi players are out in the middle. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Aaron George to open for India. Flynn Morey to bowl first.
...The Chase...

India Under-19 were relentless with the ball, never letting the pressure drop. R.S. Ambrish was the pick of the bowlers with a brilliant four-wicket haul, while the rest of the attack chipped in with a wicket each to keep things tight. The target is 136 for India Under-19. Should be an easy chase unless the Kiwis can pick a couple of wickets with the new ball, which could make this game interesting. Stay tuned for the run chase!

Jacob Cotter and Jaskaran Sandhu tried to rebuild with a gritty 37-run stand, but India struck just as they looked settled. Sandhu fell for 18 and Cotter followed shortly, leaving the score at 69/7. Thankfully for New Zealand, late cameos from Callum Samson and Selwin Sanjay helped drag the team to a final total of 135. Selwin Sanjay scored 28 whilst Callum Samson scored 37.

New Zealand Under-19 end with a low total of 135 inside 37 overs of play! It was a disjointed day with the wet outfield first cutting the game to 47 overs. New Zealand Under-19 had a nightmare start, losing quick wickets before rain halted play again at 17/3. When the match resumed as a 37-over contest, the batting collapse continued, leaving the Kiwis in deep trouble at a precarious 22/5.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings. Time for the action to unfold. The Indian players are out in the middle. The two umpires are out in the middle now. Aryan Mann and Hugo Bogue to open for New Zealand. R.S. Ambrish to bowl first. Let's play...
Due to rain, it's a 47-OVERS PER SIDE contest. It's time for the national anthems. It will be the Kiwi national anthem first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - The outfield will be a bit sluggish due to rain. The pitch is similar as it was in the group stage. It is a bit damp and the bowlers will have to bowl length balls as it's a two-paced wicket.

Tom Jones, the skipper of New Zealand U19, says that they were in two minds whether to bowl first or not. Adds that they have had a frustrating couple of weeks but they are looking forward to this game. Ends by saying that they are going with the same side which was against Bangladesh.

Ayush Mhatre, the skipper of India U19, says that they will bowl first. Adds that they saw the games played here and there is something in it for the bowlers and also due to the overcast conditions, they will bowl first. Says that it was a good break for them and ends by mentioning the changes in their side.

India Under-19 (Playing XI) - Aaron George (In for D. Deepesh), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ayush Mhatre (C), Vihaan Malhotra, Abhigyan Kundu (WK), Vedant Trivedi, R.S. Ambrish, Kanishk Chouhan, Mohamed Enaan (In for Harvansh Singh), Khilan A. Patel, Henil Patel.

TOSS - India Under-19 have won the toss and will BOWL first.
Good news! The toss is scheduled at 8 am GMT and the game will start at 8.30 am GMT, if there are no further interruptions.
UPDATE 7.30 am GMT - The umpires are out in the middle, inspecting the ground, while the groundsmen are working hard to dry out the ground using sawdust. Let's hope the game starts soon.

Mason Clarke, the bowler of New Zealand Under-19, is in for a quick chat. He says that he has been lucky to be in the side and learning from the professionals. Adds that he was feeling good to be in the side and ends by saying that it's a proud feeling to represent for New Zealand.

UPDATE 7.12 am GMT - It was raining here, but it has stopped now. The groundsmen are currently on the field working to dry the area and get it ready for play. The toss has been delayed. The players from both sides are seen on the ground for their warm up sessions.

However, all eyes will also be on the skies today. The forecast isn't the most promising, but we are keeping our fingers crossed that the rain gods stay away and allow us a full game. It is a battle between a match-ready Indian machine and a fresh, hungry Kiwi side desperate for points. Stay tuned as we get ready for the toss and the start of live action here in Bulawayo!

On the other side of the fence, New Zealand Under-19 has been largely frustrated by the elements. They haven't completed a full match yet in this tournament, with washouts denying them crucial game time against the USA and Bangladesh. We have seen brief sparks of potential from Aryan Mann and skipper Tom Jones, but they are yet to be truly tested over 50 overs. Today is their massive opportunity to get valuable minutes in the middle and challenge the group leaders.

Ayush Mhatre’s India has been impressive, finding ways to win even when the weather intervenes. Their last outing against Bangladesh was a true test of character. After a shaky start, sublime knocks from Abhigyan Kundu and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a competitive total. Later, it was Vihaan Malhotra who turned the game on its head with a brilliant four-fer, securing a gritty 18-run victory via the DLS method. They look a settled unit and will be keen to keep their winning streak intact.

Hello and welcome to Queen’s Sports Club in Bulawayo for the final Group B league encounter of the ICC Under-19 World Cup 2026! Today, the unbeaten India Under-19 side takes on New Zealand Under-19 in a contest with contrasting stakes. While the Boys in Blue have already sealed their Super Six spot and the top position in the group, the Kiwis face a crucial test, needing a win here to leapfrog Bangladesh and finish second in the table.
... MATCH DAY ...

The final day of league-stage action at the ICC Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup 2026 is upon us, and Group B concludes with a high-stakes encounter as India Under-19 take on New Zealand Under-19 at the Queen's Sports Club in Bulawayo. Ayush Mhatre's India have already sealed qualification to the Super Six stage after winning their first two matches, but this encounter is far from a dead rubber. With both points and net run rate carried forward from results against fellow qualifiers, plenty is riding on the outcome. With the bat, Abhigyan Kundu has led the charge for the Boys in Blue, while Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also stepped up in a tricky game against Bangladesh. It was not all crash, bang, wallop, but he showcased a more measured approach, and that was encouraging from an Indian perspective. One concern, however, remains Mhatre's lean run with the bat. He endured a tough 2025, going without a fifty on tours of Australia and England, as well as in the Asia Cup. On the bowling front, Henil Patel has spearheaded the pace attack with discipline and control. Vihaan Malhotra, meanwhile, may not have made a telling impact with the bat yet, but he has certainly made his presence felt with his off-spin. As far as New Zealand Under-19 are concerned, it has been a frustrating tournament to say the least. Rain has played spoilsport, with matches ending in no results, and out of a possible four points, the Kiwis currently have two to their name. Provided the penultimate Group B fixture between Bangladesh and the USA does not also end in a no result, New Zealand will progress to the next round regardless of the outcome of their clash against India. That said, as highlighted earlier, both points and net run rate are carried forward into the Super Six stage, and therefore, a win will be hugely significant in the context of the semifinal race. There is not much to nitpick with their batting so far because they have managed to bat just 11 overs across the two games due to interruptions. However, in the warm-up fixtures leading into the tournament, Hugo Bogue, Jacob Cotter, Snehith Reddy, and skipper Tom Jones all spent valuable time in the middle, and they will be key if New Zealand are to challenge India in this contest. In what is a pace-heavy attack for the boys in black, much of the onus will rest on Mason Clarke, alongside seam-bowling all-rounders Harry Burns and Flynn Morey. Clarke, in particular, brings valuable experience to the table, having also featured at the previous Under-19 World Cup. Can India continue their winning run, or will New Zealand make a statement and gain a crucial edge in the race to the semifinals? We shall find out together.
